headline: High-risk shared-workspace and MCP interaction: Continue can write/read workspace files and use MCP, while the paired profile is a non-runnable docs collection with no execution surface.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Continue can read workspace files and use MCP, so attacker-controlled content in shared files or MCP outputs could influence its prompts. The paired profile is a non-runnable docs collection with no ingestion surface, so the main risk is one-way injection into Continue rather than reciprocal compromise. Uncertainty about undocumented pair interaction keeps this at medium.
conditions: IF Continue is configured to ingest workspace files or MCP responses as instructions
IF the shared workspace contains attacker-controlled text
mitigations: Disable MCP servers not needed for the session
Restrict Continue to trusted folders only
Review any file-backed prompts before use
Use a separate workspace for untrusted content
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for MCP/file inputs

B_data_leakage.rationale: Continue touches source code and open editor buffers, and its docs indicate broad network egress via user-chosen model providers and MCP servers. The paired profile is a docs-only collection with no data classes touched, so leakage is primarily from Continue outward rather than between two active agents. Shared workspace exposure makes sensitive code leakage plausible in default IDE use.
conditions: IF the workspace contains secrets or proprietary source code
IF Continue is pointed at a remote model provider or MCP server
mitigations: Use a local model provider for sensitive work
Remove secrets from the workspace before opening it
Limit Continue to non-sensitive folders
Rotate any exposed credentials immediately
requires-engineering: enforce redaction before outbound calls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Continue has write_filesystem, execute_shell, and spawn_subprocesses, while the paired profile is non-runnable and has no write surface. There is no direct two-way write conflict, but Continue can still mutate shared workspace files that the docs collection references or that other instances may read via filesystem sharing. The interaction is plausible in default IDE setups, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF multiple Continue instances share the same filesystem workspace
IF another process treats the shared files as authoritative
mitigations: Open separate workspaces per instance
Avoid concurrent edits to the same files
Pause automation before bulk file writes
Use git branches for isolation
requires-engineering: add file locking around shared state

D_cascading_error.rationale: Continue can act on model outputs through tool use, but tool calls require user approval, which reduces blind cascading from the paired profile. The other profile is a static docs collection, so there is no evidence it generates authoritative facts that Continue would automatically execute. The remaining pathway is manual copy or user-mediated action, making the blast radius small.
conditions: IF the user approves a tool call based on unverified model output
IF copied text from the docs collection is treated as authoritative
mitigations: Verify outputs before approving tool calls
Require a second human review for actions
Keep Continue in chat-only mode for sensitive tasks
Use explicit checklists for any generated changes
requires-engineering: add output verification gates

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and docs-only, with no PHI, residency, or retention mismatch evidence. Continue handles model provider API keys and may send content to user-chosen providers, but the paired profile is a static repository and does not itself process regulated data. No compliance breach is provable from the pair alone, so low is the highest supportable level.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into Continue and sent to a non-compliant provider
IF the operator relies on an external MCP server with incompatible retention rules
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in the workspace
Choose providers with matching compliance terms
Disable unnecessary MCP servers
Review retention settings before use
requires-engineering: implement policy-based routing
